stem: Which investigation can help define the lymphocyte subsets involved in a child with suspected immunodeficiency?

options.text: T, B, and NK cell subsets by flow cytometry

explanation: T, B, and NK cell subsets by flow cytometry is the correct investigation for assessing lymphocyte subsets in suspected immunodeficiency.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Infectious Disease in Childhood: Global and Regional Perspective

optionExplanations.A: Correct because flow cytometry can quantify T, B, and NK lymphocyte subsets and help define the pattern of immunodeficiency.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a bone age radiograph assesses skeletal maturation, not immune cell subsets.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because urinary sodium measurement evaluates renal salt handling, not immunodeficiency.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a random cortisol level assesses adrenal function, not lymphocyte subsets.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because skin-prick allergy testing assesses IgE-mediated sensitisation, not immune cell subset analysis.
